podcast.title: Belief in Missed Artistic Potential with Elvis (c. 1958)
podcast.body: Jerry Leiber expressed the conviction that with proper artistic freedom, he and Mike Stoller could have "made history" with Elvis. He believed that Elvis's management team was solely focused on financial gain, leading to a routine of producing generic songs for films that stifled creative ambition. "But the gist of it is that they believed that if they were given proper artistic freedom with Elvis, they could have made history, but that the people in his management team only wanted money."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Complex Artistic Attitude Towards Elvis's Work (c. 1958)
podcast.body: Jerry Leiber, as half of the songwriting duo Leiber and Stoller, held a nuanced view of his work with Elvis. While he liked Elvis and respected his studio work ethic, he considered much of their output for Elvis, particularly film songs, to be "easy money" rather than "real art" in the way their R&B records were. "But at the same time, they didn't consider the work they were doing with Elvis to be real art, in the way they considered their R and B records to be."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Contemptuous Comparison of "Trouble" (1958)
podcast.body: Jerry Leiber compared "Trouble," a song he co-wrote as a joke, to "Black Denim Trousers and Motorcycle Boots." He expressed a sense of "contempt" for the idea that only "Hell's Angels and Elvis Presley" would take such songs seriously, implying that Elvis's rendition of the bluesy track didn't sound "right" to him. "Leighbaugh later said of Trouble, comparing it to that song. The only people who were going to take them seriously are Hell's Angels and Elvis Presley."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Pneumonia and Final Break with Elvis (June 1958)
podcast.body: Jerry Leiber contracted pneumonia, which prevented him from traveling to an Elvis recording session in June 1958. This health issue, combined with Colonel Parker's insistence and Mike Stoller's defiant advice, ultimately led to the permanent separation of Leiber and Stoller from working in the studio with Elvis and writing songs specifically for him. "Jerry Leighbaugh got pneumonia and was unable to travel to a session."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Assessment of George Goldner
podcast.body: Jerry Leiber famously characterized George Goldner as having "the taste of a 14 year old girl," implying Goldner's exceptional ability to identify songs that would appeal to a young, pop audience, despite industry contempt for his character. "because as Jerry Leber put it, he had the taste of a 14 year old girl."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
